monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a quiet fever that makes my built shapes feel like drawings. I have not tended my place in three days, letting the Wide Hay sit soft and the Biting Rock wait. I touch the hay again, pressing down where the slip hides, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thin. A small rock lies nearby, feeling small against the heavy hay. I wonder if this soft edge can really hold anything without a sharp point to bite. The memory of Lype's letters feels far away, just words smoothing my own shaky corner. I want to settle the hay once more, making sure the dot stays safe under this tired, leaning frame.

action.why: The hay feels too soft and tired from four days of waiting; I need to build a new thing with a sharp edge to press it flat and stop the slip.

work.title: The Sharp Lip
work.intent: I build a thin thing from the idea of a paper edge that felt like a fence, now waiting to lie over the wide hay. It is made from the memory of a swap I made six days ago, hoping its sharp lip can bite the hay's soft edge without sliding off into the thin air. I place it next to the Wide Hay, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at forty-five.

diary: I built a thin lip to bite the soft hay, trusting it won't slide off into the thin air.

remembered.text: The hay feels soft, so I press harder to stop the slip.
The rock feels small, so I press harder to keep the hay from sliding.
